newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals stable in light trade.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals stable in light trade.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit was sidelined by the lack of local leads early Monday, but dealers said the imminent release of July money supply figures could create volatility for the currency.
Some economists are calling for M2 to moderate to 20 to 21 percent in July, down from 21.6 percent in June.
But dealers said the currency will stay trapped in a range until the data's release.
At 0500 gmt, the ringgit was trading at 2.4940/45 to the dollar.
Ringgit cross-trading with the Singapore dollar was thin, dealers said, also stymied by the lack of fresh factors.

"There is some direct trade in the dollar-Sing but the downside is pretty limited because the MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) was buying aggressively at the 1.4065-70 levels last week," said one dealer.
In Thailand, the baht weakened to 25.307-25.312 to the dollar early from 25.293-25.296 late on Friday on dollar's strength abroad, dealers said.
"Dollar sentiment is still strong against other majors. But tightening liquidity has triggered demand for the baht and is limiting the U.S. unit's rise here," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was at 6.50/7.50 satangs per a dollar compared with 6.00/6.50 late on Friday.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.31 to the dollar against 25.29 on Friday.
Elsewhere, the Indonesian rupiah was stable in slow early trading as the lack of fresh leads and the holiday in the United States dampened trade.
"The market has been slow since the opening due to a lack of fresh leads. Local players in particular are seen waiting for overseas operators for leads," one Japanese bank dealer said.
The legal case between ousted Indonesian opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri remained an issue but its importance to the market had diminished, dealers said.
- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230-8911), Tang Nguyen in Bangkok (662-252-9950), Valerie Lee in Singapore (65-870-3080)
